# Caching in Computer Systems

Caching is one of the most important ideas in computer systems. It is a technique used to store copies of frequently accessed data in a faster location so that future requests can be served more quickly. Although the basic idea is simple, caching appears throughout computing: in processors, operating systems, databases, web browsers, content delivery networks, and distributed systems. Its purpose is always the same: to reduce latency, improve throughput, and make better use of limited resources.

At its core, caching exploits a fundamental property of computer programs known as locality of reference. Programs tend to access the same data repeatedly or access data that is close to what they have recently used.
